tutorials.title: Battery draining quickly
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Battery draining quickly

Excessive power depletion can severely impact device performance, daily usability, and long-term hardware health. Identifying the root causes of rapid power loss helps you resolve background process conflicts, optimize energy settings, and restore your device to normal operational capacity.

steps.text:
If your device battery is draining quickly, there are several steps you can take to try and fix the problem.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Manage your battery
Manage your background apps
Adjust your auto-lock and brightness preferences

steps.heading: Manage your battery
steps.text:
Within the Settings app's Battery & charging section, you can:
View which apps and system components are using the most battery life
View your overall battery usage statistics
Check your Overcharge protection settings
Enable Battery Saver mode
Together, these features should help you get a better sense of how your battery is being used and whether you're charging your device optimally for long-term battery health.

steps.heading: Manage your background apps
steps.text:
Managing your background apps prevents unused software from silently running, tracking location, or fetching data when you aren't using it.
Putting these apps to sleep stops unnecessary processor activity, directly reducing constant power drain on your device.
links: Managing app power usage and force closing apps
options: Next: Adjust your auto-lock and brightness preferences

steps.heading: Adjust your auto-lock and brightness preferences
steps.text:
Adjusting your auto-lock and brightness preferences reduces display power draw, which is the single largest consumer of battery life on a phone.
Shortening the screen timeout and dimming screen intensity ensures your display isn't draining energy when you aren't actively looking at it.
links: Adjusting the screen timeout and brightness

tutorials.title: Can't connect to Wi-Fi or internet
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Can't connect to Wi-Fi or internet

Loss of network connectivity disrupts online communication, daily operations, and remote access to essential tools. Diagnosing link failures helps restore online functionality, resolve router communication conflicts, and re-establish stable signal transmission.

steps.text:
If you are unable to connect to a Wi-Fi network or hotspot, or if you're encountering slowdowns on your existing connection, there are several actions you can try to fix the problem.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Make sure airplane mode is off
Connect to Wi-Fi
Forget and Reconnect to Wi-Fi
Restart your device
Restart your Wi-Fi router / modem
Reset your network settings
options: Next: Make sure airplane mode is off

steps.heading: Make sure airplane mode is off
steps.text:
Turning off Airplane Mode re-enables your phone's Wi-Fi, cellular data, and Bluetooth radios to restore your device's connection to the internet.
Toggling it on and off also forces the phone to drop stale connection states and re-establish a fresh, clean link with local cell towers and network routers.
links: Turning Airplane mode on and off

steps.heading: Connect to Wi-Fi
steps.text:
Within the Settings app, take a moment to confirm that your phone is connected to a Wi-Fi network. A icon will indicate an active connection to whatever Wi-Fi network you've tapped on (or previously saved).
Note: If you're successfully connected to Wi-Fi, but you're getting a "No Internet Connection" message, there may be an issue with your Wi-Fi router/gateway that you'll need to troubleshoot.
options: Next: Forget and Reconnect to Wi-Fi

steps.heading: Forget and Reconnect to Wi-Fi
steps.text:
Forgetting and reconnecting to Wi-Fi wipes out saved network credentials, IP settings, and cached security handshake data for that specific router on your phone.
These settings can be found within the Network & internet section of your Settings app. From there, tap Saved Networks, and you'll be able to forget the Wi-Fi network. Reconnect, enter your password, and see if that fixes your issue.

steps.heading: Try restarting your device
steps.text: Restarting your phone clears stuck network drivers and flushes temporary system memory. This can clear temporary software glitches and forces your phone to establish a fresh, stable connection to the internet.
links: Turning your phone on and off
options: Next: Restart your Wi-Fi router / modem

steps.heading: Restart your Wi-Fi router / modem
steps.text: Restarting your Wi-Fi router or modem clears its temporary memory and fixes local IP address assignment conflicts. This gives your phone a fresh, clean network path to reconnect without affecting any saved settings on your phone.

steps.heading: Reset your network settings
steps.text:
Resetting your network settings clears out your phone's saved connection info and lets it start fresh, often fixing problems that Airplane Mode or a restart couldn't.
Before you reset, write down anything you'll need to re-enter, since this action erases:
Wi-Fi passwords
Bluetooth pairings
VPN settings
APN (Access Point Name) settings, if you entered these manually to connect to your carrier's cellular network
You'll be able to resync your Wi-Fi passwords, but the other settings will need to be entered again.
If you had to enter APN settings manually to access a cellular network, you'll need to do that again before attempting a phone call.

tutorials.title: Can't install an app
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Can't install an app

Software installation failures block new software deployment and keep critical tools from launching. Troubleshooting setup errors helps identify storage shortages, bypass permission restrictions, and resolve package corruption so applications run properly.

steps.text:
If you are unable to install an app, there are several steps you can take to try to fix the problem.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Check your mobile or Wi-Fi signal
Check your available storage
Restart your device
options: Next: Check your cellular or Wi-Fi signal

steps.heading: Check your connection
steps.text:
Check the cellular signal status icon in the upper-right corner of your device. Generally, the more bars that are displayed, the better the connection; if you have low or no signal, connectivity issues may be the reason why you're having issues downloading an app.
If you're connected to Wi-Fi, you'll also be able to view your signal strength in the same area. If no Wi-fi icon is shown, you may need to connect to a Wi-fi network. If your Wi-fi icon has an exclamation point, there is a problem with your connection.

steps.heading: Check your available storage
steps.text:
You'll want to confirm that your phone has enough space required beyond the app’s listed size, which you can typically do within Settings > Storage.
If your free space drops below a safe threshold (typically 10–15%), your operating system may automatically block downloads to prevent system errors.

steps.heading: Try restarting your device
steps.text:
Restarting your phone clears frozen background download queues and flushes corrupted temporary system memory that causes downloads to stall on "Pending."
It also forces fresh network and account authentication connections with the app store servers so the download can start from a clean slate.
links: Turning your phone on and off

Can't make or receive calls

If you're connected to Wi-Fi, you'll also be able to view your signal strength in the same area. Enabling Wi-Fi calling may help you place phone calls in areas with limited or no cellular coverage.

steps.heading: Use Airplane Mode to reset your connection
steps.text:
Sometimes your phone shows a strong signal or Wi-Fi connection, but calls still won't go through. Airplane Mode may clear this up without a full restart.
Turning on Airplane Mode disconnects your phone's wireless radios, cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth. When you turn it back off, your phone re-registers with the nearest cell tower from scratch, rather than continuing to use whatever connection it had before.
To try this:
Turn on Airplane Mode.
Wait about 15 seconds.
Turn Airplane Mode off.

steps.text:
If you're still having issues making a phone call on your device, contact your carrier for additional support. They can help identify whether an issue on their end is affecting your calls (for example, a problem with your account, your SIM, or a local cell tower).
It's also possible your device has a hardware issue. To check, run a hardware test in the Device Help app, which comes preinstalled on your Motorola phone. It can help you pinpoint the problem and figure out what to do next.

tutorials.title: Can't pair with Bluetooth device
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Can't pair with Bluetooth device

Pairing errors prevent essential wireless peripherals and accessories from communicating properly with your hardware. Clearing connection bottlenecks and resetting radio protocols ensures seamless device discovery, uninterrupted transmission, and stable short-range link performance.

steps.text:
If you are unable to pair with a Bluetooth device, there are several actions you can try to fix the problem.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Turn Bluetooth off and on
Pair with a bluetooth device
Unpair or forget a bluetooth device
Restart your device
Reset Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Settings
options: Next: Turn Bluetooth off and on
substeps: Turn Bluetooth off and on
Pair with a bluetooth device
Unpair or forget a bluetooth device

steps.heading: Turn Bluetooth off and on
steps.text: Under Connection preferences within Connected Devices you will find your Bluetooth settings. Once there, use the toggle to turn your Bluetooth on and off, which will allow your devices to attempt reconnecting and potentially fix your issue.
options: Next: Pair with a different bluetooth device

steps.heading: Pair with a different bluetooth device
steps.text:
Pairing your phone with another bluetooth device can help you further diagnose and isolate the core issue.
If the secondary device connects fine. Your phone’s Bluetooth hardware and software are working. The issue is specific to the original device (e.g., its battery is low, it’s not in true pairing mode, or it needs a firmware update).
Scenario B: The secondary device also fails to pair. The root cause is inside your phone (or its software settings).
options: Next: Unpair or forget your bluetooth device

steps.heading: Unpair or forget your bluetooth device
steps.text: Within your Connected devices you will be able to access your device's settings that you want to forget. Forgetting a Bluetooth device wipes out the outdated or broken passkey your phone saved, allowing both devices to reattempt a working connection from scratch.

steps.heading: Try restarting your device
steps.text: Manually restarting your device closes out frozen apps and clears out clogged background memory, giving the phone's entire operating system a clean slate to send and receive wireless signals properly again.
links: Turning your phone on and off
options: Next: Reset Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Settings

steps.heading: Reset your Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Settings
steps.text: Resetting Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings completely clears out all your saved wireless passwords, network configurations, and paired accessories, forcing your phone's wireless system back to its factory-fresh starting state.

tutorials.title: Can't send or receive email

Moto G - 2025
Can't send or receive email

Communication disruptions in electronic messaging stall important correspondence and lead to missed notifications. Checking transmission protocols and server configurations clears stuck queues, corrects sync errors, and ensures seamless message routing.

steps.text:
If you are unable to send and receive email messages, there are steps you can try to fix the problem.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Make sure airplane mode is off
Check your mobile or Wi-Fi signal
Force Stop & Clear your App Cache
Restart your device
Check your email account settings
Remove and re-add email account
options: Next: Make sure Airplane Mode is off

steps.heading: Make sure airplane mode is off
steps.text:
Turning off Airplane Mode re-enables your phone's Wi-Fi, cellular data, and Bluetooth radios to restore your device's connection to the internet, which may be a reason why you can't send or receive email.
Toggling it on and off also forces the phone to drop stale connection states and re-establish a fresh, clean link with local cell towers and network routers.
links: Turning Airplane mode on and off

steps.heading: Check your connection
steps.text:
Check the cellular signal status icon in the upper-right corner of your device. Generally, the more bars that are displayed, the better the connection; if you have low or no signal, that may be the reason why you're experiencing issues sending or receiving email.
If you're connected to Wi-Fi, you'll also be able to view your signal strength in the same area. If no Wi-fi icon is shown, you may need to connect to a Wi-fi network. If your Wi-fi icon has an exclamation point, there is a problem with your connection.
options: Next: Force stop and clear your app cache

steps.heading: Force Stop & Clear your App Cache
steps.text:
Clearing the app cache wipes corrupted temporary background files and broken sync indexes without deleting your email account or personal data.
Force-stopping the app fully shuts down any stuck or frozen background processes so your email app can initiate a clean reconnection to the servers when reopened.
Long-press your email app on your device, pull up App Info, and tap Force stop. Then, relaunch your email app. You can also clear the app cache on this screen.
links: Clearing the cache and data for an individual app

steps.heading: Try restarting your device
steps.text: Restarting your device clears frozen app processes, flushes temporary system memory, and forces a fresh connection to your cellular or Wi-Fi network.
options: Next: Check your email account settings

steps.heading: Check your email account settings
steps.text:
Take a moment to make sure your login details and other options are correct, so your phone can properly send and receive messages.
These Account Settings are typically found in your Settings app > Passwords & accounts.
options: Next: Remove and re-add your email account

steps.heading: Remove and re-add your email account
steps.text:
Removing and re-adding your email account clears out broken security tokens, password mismatches, and corrupted server connection profiles on your phone.
It forces the phone to re-authenticate with the right email servers and download fresh, correct incoming and outgoing server settings from scratch.
Within the Passwords & Accounts section of your Settings app, tap Add account after you have removed your account to re-add it.

steps.heading: No signal or data connection
steps.text: Check the top of your screen for signal bars. Try temporarily turning off Wi-Fi to confirm you have at least a usable cellular signal, since a weak or absent cellular connection can block texts even if Wi-Fi is working fine.

steps.heading: Airplane mode is on
steps.text: Check and confirm Airplane mode is turned off. If it's on, your phone may not be able to receive any texts until it's turned off.

steps.heading: The message is too large
steps.text: Photos, videos, or long group threads sometimes fail to send as a regular text. Try removing the attachment or shortening the message, then send it again to see if that works.

steps.heading: Make sure the recipient isn't blocked
steps.text: Check your messaging app's blocked contacts list to confirm the recipient isn't on it.

Can't turn device on or off

If you're having issues powering your phone off or on, there are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot the problem.

Force restart a frozen or unresponsive phone
Are you having issues powering off your phone, or powering it on?

steps.heading: Powering off
steps.text:
To power off your phone, first try one of these two methods.
1) Physical buttons
Press and hold the Power button until the power menu appears, then tap Power off.
If holding the Power button opens Google Gemini instead, press and hold Power and Volume Up together until the power menu appears.
2) Quick Settings
Swipe down twice from the top of the screen to fully open Quick Settings, tap the Power icon, then tap Power off.
If neither of these work, continue to the next step to force restart your phone.
links: Turning your phone on and off

steps.heading: Force-restart
steps.text:
If you're still having trouble and the previous steps didn't help, the next step is to force-restart.
Press and hold the Power button and the Volume Up button at the same time.
Continue holding for about 7–10 seconds, past any menu that appears.
Release when you feel a vibration or see the logo appear.
Wait for the device to finish restarting.

Mobile Hotspot isn't working

Learn how to fix a personal hotspot that won’t connect. Follow this step-by-step user manual to troubleshoot connection drops, password issues, and cellular data errors.

steps.text:
Mobile Hotspot allows you to broadcast a Wi-Fi network from your phone based on your cellular connection.
If you're having issues setting up or using Mobile Hotspot, there are a few ways you can troubleshoot the issue.
Within this guide, you'll learn how to:
Make sure mobile hotspot is properly set up
Restart your phone
Check for updates
Check your cellular connection

steps.heading: Setting up Mobile Hotspot
steps.text:
Take a moment to check that Mobile Hotspot is enabled on your device. You'll also want to confirm that your carrier and service plan supports Wi-Fi hotspots, or else the feature may not appear (or you may not be able to enable it).
Typically, to set up a hotspot:
Go to Settings > Network & internet > Hotspot & tethering > Mobile Hotspot, then turn on Use Wi-Fi hotspot.
Make sure mobile data is turned on. Go to Settings > Network & internet and check that the Mobile data toggle is on.
If devices have trouble connecting, go to Mobile Hotspot > Speed & compatibility and select 2.4 GHz. (You may need to turn Wi-Fi off and back on on your other devices before they can connect to your hotspot.)
You can also try forgetting the Wi-Fi network on your connecting device and reconnecting to your Mobile Hotspot, in case you accidentally saved an incorrect password or are encountering some other kind of connection issue.

steps.heading: Try restarting your phone
steps.text:
Restarting your phone is a quick, low-risk first step that can resolve many Mobile Hotspot issues. To restart your phone, try one of these two methods.
1) Physical buttons
Press and hold the Power button until the power menu appears, then tap Restart.
If holding the Power button opens Google Gemini instead, press and hold Power and Volume Up together until the power menu appears.
2) Quick Settings
Swipe down twice from the top of the screen to fully open Quick Settings, tap the Power icon, then tap Restart.
If neither of these work, continue to the next step to force restart your phone.

steps.heading: Check for updates
steps.text: Next, you'll want to make sure your phone is running the latest version of Android, just in case that's somehow preventing you from using the Mobile Hotspot feature.
links: Checking for and installing system updates

steps.heading: Checking your cellular connection
steps.text:
It's possible that devices can connect to your Mobile Hotspot, but you have a weak or problematic cellular connection that's affecting your devices' performance.
Try turning off your Mobile Hotspot temporarily and use your phone as you normally would. Make sure you're not connected to a Wi-Fi network and try placing a call or loading a webpage.
If you're encountering issues, try switching your phone to Airplane Mode, waiting 15 seconds, and turning it off. Otherwise, try moving to a location with a stronger or more consistent cellular signal and testing Mobile Hotspot again to see if the issue is with your phone's connection or the hotspot.

options: Next: Check Wi-Fi Calling is turned on

steps.heading: Check that Wi-Fi calling is turned on
steps.text:
First, let's confirm that Wi-Fi calling is turned on. You can find this setting in a couple of places.
To check:
Open the Phone app and tap More options (⋮) in the top corner.
Tap Settings > Calling accounts
Select your carrier or SIM, then tap Wi-Fi calling.
Check that Use Wi-Fi calling is turned on. If it's off, tap the toggle to turn it on.
If you don't see this option there, try:
Settings app > Network & internet > SIMs and mobile network > your SIM > Wi-Fi calling
Note: Wi-Fi calling availability depends on your carrier and plan. If you don't see the option in either place, your plan may not support it on your phone.
options: Next: Confirm you're connected to Wi-Fi

steps.heading: Confirm you're connected to Wi-Fi
steps.text: Wi-Fi Calling requires an active Wi-Fi connection. Check the Wi-Fi icon in your status bar and make sure you're connected to a working network, not just cellular data.
options: Next: Check if Airplane Mode is enabled

steps.heading: Toggle Airplane Mode on and off
steps.text: Turn Airplane Mode on for 10 seconds, then turn it off. This resets your device's network connections, including Wi-Fi and cellular radios.
links: Turning Airplane mode on and off

steps.heading: Update your emergency address
steps.text:
Wi-Fi calling uses this address to send emergency services to your location if you dial 911, so it's important to keep it current.
To update it:
Open the Phone app and tap More options (⋮).
Tap Settings > Calling accounts.
Tap your SIM or carrier, then tap Wi-Fi calling.
Tap Emergency address to review or update it.

steps.heading: Restart your device
steps.text: Power your device off completely, wait 10 seconds, then turn it back on. This clears temporary network glitches that can block Wi-Fi Calling from connecting.

steps.heading: Check for carrier or software updates
steps.text: Go to Settings > System Updates to install any pending updates, and check with your carrier that Wi-Fi Calling is active on your line.
links: Checking for and installing system updates
options: Next: Reseat your SIM card (if applicable)

steps.heading: Remove and reinsert your SIM card
steps.text:
Note: This step only applies to devices with a physical SIM card. If your device uses an eSIM instead, skip to the next step.
Power off your device, remove the SIM card, wait a few seconds, then reinsert it firmly. This can resolve issues where your carrier isn't properly recognizing your account.
links: Inserting and removing the nano SIM card

steps.heading: Reset your network settings
steps.text:
Resetting your network settings clears out your phone's saved connection info and lets it start fresh, often fixing problems that Airplane Mode or a restart couldn't.
Before you reset, write down anything you'll need to re-enter, since this action erases:
Wi-Fi passwords
Bluetooth pairings
VPN settings
APN (Access Point Name) settings, if you entered these manually to connect to your carrier's cellular network
You'll be able to resync your Wi-Fi passwords, but the other settings will need to be entered again.
If you had to enter APN settings manually to access a cellular network, you'll need to do that again before attempting a phone call.

steps.heading: Get additional support
steps.text: If you're still having issues with Wi-Fi Calling on your device, you should contact your carrier for additional support. They'll be able to help identify if there's an issue on their end that's affecting Wi-Fi Calling (e.g. a problem with your account, your SIM, or your Wi-Fi Calling eligibility).

Use these steps to learn how to navigate to a list of previously installed apps that were previously on your device so you can reinstall or enable again.

steps.text: From the Play Store app main screen, tap the Account icon.

notes:
Note: 

From this screen, you can review a list of apps that were once installed but aren’t currently.

steps.text: Tap the app you'd like to download.

tutorials.title: Removing an account
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Removing an account

You are able to remove any email accounts that you have set up on your device. Removing an email account from your device does not delete the email account.

steps.text: From within the Settings app, scroll to and tap Passwords, passkeys & accounts.
Select the account you'd like to remove.

tutorials.title: Removing apps and widgets from the Home screen
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Removing apps and widgets from the Home screen

Remove unused widgets to free up room on the home screen of your device. Widgets can be added back later if needed.

steps.text: From the Home screen, touch and hold the widget you'd like to remove.
notes:
Note: 

For this tutorial, we're removing a widget. The steps to remove an app are the same.

tutorials.title: Reporting a third-party developer issue in Google Play

steps.text: From the app you want to report, scroll to and tap App support.
notes:
Note: 

From here, you will find the developer's contact information. You can then contact the developer directly regarding any issues, refunds, etc.

tutorials.title: Reporting inappropriate or infringing content in Google Play

steps.text: From the app you want to report, tap the Menu icon.
Select your reasoning for the report.

notes:
Note: 

Depending on your selection, you may be prompted to enter in a description for your complaint.

tutorials.title: Resetting all settings
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Resetting all settings

A common troubleshooting step is resetting all of your apps to their factory defaults if you are having trouble with your device; your personal information will not be deleted.

steps.text: From the Settings app, scroll to and tap System.

notes:
Note: 

Resetting your app preferences will reset all customized settings on your phone. Personal information will not be deleted.

tutorials.title: Resetting network settings
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Resetting network settings

If you are having trouble connecting to the Internet you may need to reset your network connections. Resetting your network connections will disconnect any Bluetooth devices connected to your device and disconnect your device from any Wi-Fi networks it is connected to.

steps.text: From the Settings app, scroll to and tap System.
Tap Reset Mobile Network Settings and follow the on-screen prompts to successfully reset.
notes:
Note: 

Resetting your network settings will reset all your Wi-Fi, cellular, and VPN settings.

tutorials.title: Resetting your Google Account password
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Resetting your Google Account password

You can change your password if you have forgotten your password or have another reason to change it. Using a strong password can help keep your account information safe. Using at least eight characters and adding capitalization and symbols can help strengthen your password.

steps.text: From any Google sign-in screen, enter the email address for an account you'd like to reset your password for and tap Next.
notes:
Note: 

If you do not know your email address, tap Forgot email? and follow the instructions to recover your address.

Note: 

If you have other Account Recovery options set for your account, you may be prompted to provide a different verification method.

steps.text: Enter the verification code sent to your recovery email or phone number and tap Next.
Enter your new password into both entry fields and tap Save password.

tutorials.title: Restarting your phone
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Restarting your phone

Learn how to turn your device off and back on again. Restarting your device is often the first step when troubleshooting a device issue.

steps.text: From the Home screen, press and hold the Power button.
notes:
Note: 

For your device, you may have to hold Power and Volume Up.

tutorials.title: Reviewing your Google Play transaction history

steps.text: From the Play Store app main screen, tap the Account icon.

tutorials.title: Saving split-screen app layouts
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Saving split-screen app layouts

Learn how to save certain split-screen app layouts to your home screen.

steps.text: With your split-screen desired apps running in the background, tap the Recent apps icon.
Select the other app you want to have as part of the split-screen.
Tap one of the icons for the apps that are in split-screen mode.

tutorials.title: Searching locally
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Searching locally

You can search for restaurants or other businesses that are near you and then filter them based on criteria such as rating or price.

steps.text: From the Google Maps main screen, tap the Search here field and enter a search term.
Swipe to and tap More filters.
Select your preferences and tap Apply.
notes:
Note: 

From here, you can filter your search results to only show the locations you're interested in. For this tutorial, we're filtering the search results by type. You can choose any filter, but steps may vary based on choice.

steps.text: Tap Directions to get directions to your destination.

tutorials.title: Secure your phone with Advanced Protection
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Secure your phone with Advanced Protection

Advanced Protection helps defend against online attacks, harmful apps, insecure connections, and other threats that put your data at risk.

steps.text: From the Settings app, scroll to and tap Security & privacy.
Scroll to and tap Advanced Protection.
Tap or slide the Device protection switch to ON.

tutorials.title: Sending a text with an attachment
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Sending a text with an attachment

Compose and send a standard SMS message with your device's text messaging app. You can send a text message to an individual or a group.

steps.text: From the Home screen, tap Messages.
When you're finished, tap the Send icon.

tutorials.title: Sending an audio message
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Sending an audio message

Discover how to send a text message with your voice using the speech to text feature on your device.

steps.text: From the Messages app main screen, tap Start chat.
Tap the Microphone icon to start recording your message.
notes:
Note: 

If necessary, follow the onscreen prompts to give Messages the appropriate permissions.

steps.text: When you're finished, tap the Stop recording icon.
When you're finished, tap the Send icon.

tutorials.title: Set your default SIM for calls, texts, and cellular data
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Set your default SIM for calls, texts, and cellular data

Discover how to configure your phone's default SIM settings. This guide covers selecting your primary SIM for making calls, sending texts, and accessing cellular data, streamlining your dual-SIM experience.

steps.text: From the Settings app, tap Network & internet.
Edit the following settings to set your SIM preferences:
notes:
Note:
Calls - Select which SIM you'd like to use by default for voice calls—or choose Ask me every time to be prompted each time you make a call.
Text - Select your default SIM for sending text messages.
Mobile data - Tap SIM for mobile data, then select on SIM to be active for mobile data. If a default is already set, you’ll see a notification letting you know.
Calls - Select which SIM you'd like to use by default for voice calls—or choose Ask me every time to be prompted each time you make a call.
Text - Select your default SIM for sending text messages.
Mobile data - Tap SIM for mobile data, then select on SIM to be active for mobile data. If a default is already set, you’ll see a notification letting you know.

tutorials.title: Setting an app timer
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting an app timer

Learn how to set app timers on your device, which give you a way to set a maximum goal for how much time you'd like to spend in a particular app each day.

steps.text: From within the Settings app, scroll to and tap Digital Wellbeing & parental controls.
Select the app you'd like to set a timer for.
Select your desired amount of time.

tutorials.title: Setting app limits for family members
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting app limits for family members

You can set up your child's device to have content restrictions. The restrictions can be on anything from websites to music or podcasts.

steps.text: From the Google Family Link app's Screen time tab, tap Time limits.
Select the app that you want to edit the privileges of.
Tap Done to save your changes.

tutorials.title: Setting screen security
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting screen security

Screen locks secure your device and protect your device from being accessed by other people. Removing your security lock will allow anyone to be able to access your device. Note that if your device is requesting a PUK code, you will need to contact your carrier to unlock your device.

steps.text: From the Settings app, scroll to and tap Security & privacy.

notes:
Note: 

For this tutorial, we're showing how to set up a PIN. You can select a different type of security, but steps may vary based on what you choose.

Note: 

Your PIN must be at least 4 numbers long.

Note: 

Tap Don't show notifications at all to prevent the content of emails, texts and other notifications from appearing on the Lock screen. You'll be notified that you have a new message, but not shown what the message contains.

tutorials.title: Setting the phone to silent
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting the phone to silent

When your device is in do not disturb or silent mode, it will not make a sound to notify you of incoming notifications.

steps.text: From the Home screen, drag down the Notification panel.
Drag down the Quick settings panel.
Tap Do Not Disturb to set your phone to silent.

tutorials.title: Setting up Call Forwarding
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting up Call Forwarding

Set up call forwarding on your device to have incoming calls routed to another number. Depending on your device you may be able to route calls differently based on whether your line is busy or not.

steps.text: From the Home screen, tap the Phone icon.
Enter a phone number you wish to forward your calls to.

tutorials.title: Setting up Gemini™
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting up Gemini™

You can ask the Google Assistant to send emails, send texts, or start phone calls for you. In order to use the Google Assistant it needs to be set up first.

steps.text: From the Home screen, tap Gemini.
notes:
Note: 

You must be signed in to a Google account to use Gemini.

tutorials.title: Setting up Moto Actions
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting up Moto Actions

You can turn on Moto Actions to give you access to shortcuts for using your device. For example you can turn the flashlight on or off using a predefined motion.

steps.text: From the Home screen, tap the Moto folder.

notes:
Note: 

If necessary, follow the prompts on the next page.

steps.text: Tap or slide the Pick up to silence switch to On.
notes:
Note: 

Tap Try it out to learn more about this feature.

tutorials.title: Setting up Screen Time as a parent
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting up Screen Time as a parent

You can set up your child's device to manage their screen time. Depending on your device, you may be able to set a daily screen time limit or limit the time a child can spend in an app.

steps.text: From the Google Family Link app's Screen time tab, tap Time limits.
Select the day you want to edit the usage limit for the child's device.
Tap or slide the Daily limit switch to ON.

tutorials.title: Setting up Voicemail
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting up Voicemail

Learn how to set up Voicemail so that you can store messages from calls you missed. If your Voicemail Icon does not appear try restarting your phone.

steps.text: While in the Phone app, a method to set up voicemail is by calling your voicemail inbox. To try this, tap the Keypad icon.
notes:
Note: 

This tutorial steps through how to activate visual voicemail. This option may not be available, depending on your cellular plan.

steps.text: Press and hold the 1 key on the dial pad and follow along with the menu prompts to complete setting up your voicemail.
notes:
Note: 

You may also be able to dial your own phone number to call your voicemail.

steps.text: Another method to setup your voicemail in the Phone app is in settings. While in the app, tap the Menu icon.
Tap or slide the Visual voicemail toggle to ON.
Tap Voicemail number to verify it's correct, or enter it if the field is blank.
notes:
Note: 

This tutorial steps through how to record a Voicemail greeting.

tutorials.title: Setting up a new phone manually
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting up a new phone manually

When you get a new device or reset your current one, follow these initial setup steps to activate and configure your device.

notes:
Note: 

Here you can change your locale, accessibility settings, and make an emergency call.

steps.text: Enter your network password, and tap Connect.
Enter your Google account's email address and tap Next.
Enter your password and tap Next.
Enter a PIN number, and tap Next.
notes:
Note: 

On this screen you can enter a PIN that you can use to lock and unlock your device.

steps.text: Re-enter your PIN number, and tap Confirm.

notes:
Note: 

On this screen you can set up fingerprint recognition for your device.

steps.text: To set up your phone as a new device, tap Do it later.
notes:
Note: 

You can also transfer apps and data from your previous phone.

steps.text: Tap Go to my home screen.

tutorials.title: Setting up an eSIM using a QR Code or Activation Code
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting up an eSIM using a QR Code or Activation Code

This tutorial guides you through the process of activating and setting up an eSIM on your smartphone using a QR code after the initial device setup has been completed. Whether you skipped eSIM activation during the initial setup or are switching carriers, this step-by-step guide will cover scanning your carrier-provided QR code and properly activating your eSIM.

steps.text: From the Settings app, tap Network & internet.
Scan the QR code with your device or tap Enter activation code to continue.
notes:
Note: 

If you choose to enter your details manually, your activation code is typically included near your QR code.

tutorials.title: Setting up an eSIM with a push notification after device setup
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting up an eSIM with a push notification after device setup

This tutorial walks you through the process of setting up an eSIM on your device using a push notification sent by your carrier. This guide shows you how to accept the notification, download the eSIM profile, and activate your mobile service quickly and securely—without scanning a QR code or manually entering details.

steps.text: From the Home screen, drag down the Notification panel.
Tap the Set up your Carrier eSIM notification.
Tap Settings to go to your network settings to activate your eSIM.
Tap or slide the switch of the eSIM you wish to activate to ON.

tutorials.title: Setting up mobile hotspot
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting up mobile hotspot

Set up your device as a Mobile Hotspot so you can share your data connection with other devices. Your device will create a Wi-Fi hotspot with its data connection. Other devices will be able to connect to the Wi-Fi hotspot.
tutorials.category: Wi-Fi, Mobile Data, Bluetooth, and Browsers

steps.text: From the Settings app, tap Network & Internet.
Tap or slide the Use Wi-Fi hotspot switch to On.
notes:
Note: 

The Configure screen lets you choose the type of security you want. You can also find your device password here.

tutorials.title: Setting up parental controls
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting up parental controls

As a parent, you can control how your child's smartphone is used, including limiting screen time and access to apps.

steps.text: From the Settings app, scroll to and tap Digital Wellbeing & parental controls.
Scroll to your child's account under Parental controls.
notes:
Note: 

If your child already has a Google account, it will show up here. If not, you will need to create one for them first before proceeding.

Note: 

You may need to sign into your own Google account to access Google Family Link.

tutorials.title: Setting up personal email
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting up personal email

Set up your personal email account on your device so that you can access your email messages, send new emails and more. You can have mutliple email accounts on your device.

steps.text: From the Home screen, tap the Google folder.

notes:
Note: 

In this tutorial, we're using a Mail.com account. You can use a different account, but steps may vary based on what you choose.

steps.text: Enter your email address or phone number.

tutorials.title: Setting up your second cellular plan with an eSIM
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting up your second cellular plan with an eSIM

Adding a secondary eSIM alongside a physical SIM or eSIM allows you to quickly switch between two cellular plans and/or carriers for voice or data.

steps.text: From the Settings app, tap Network & internet.

notes:
Note: 

You may see a slightly different screen if your phone is already using an eSIM.

steps.text: Place the QR code provided by your carrier within the camera frame.
notes:
Note: 

Your Device's camera automatically detects QR codes. If your carrier didn't provide a code, you may need to use their app to purchase a cellular plan.

steps.text: Select the eSIM that was just added.
Tap or slide the Use this SIM switch to ON.

tutorials.title: Setting your volume levels with the volume panel
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Setting your volume levels with the volume panel

Learn how to adjust the volume of your device.

steps.text: Press the Volume buttons to change your volume.

notes:
Note: 

From this screen, the volumes for various functions of your phone can be adjusted.

Note: 

For this tutorial, we're adjusting the ring volume. Other volumes that can be changed include the volumes of your alarms, notifications, calls, and media.

tutorials.title: Sharing Photos
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Sharing Photos

Share photos and videos with others via Bluetooth, text message, email, Facebook and more.

steps.text: From the Home screen, tap Photos.
Select the photo you'd like to share.

notes:
Note: 

For this tutorial, we're sharing photos with Bluetooth. You can select any available share option, but steps may vary slightly depending on what you choose.

Note: 

Make sure the device you're sending photos to has Bluetooth on and is set to be discoverable or visible. Once another device is selected, your picture will automatically send.

tutorials.title: Sharing photos
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Sharing photos

Share photos and videos with others via Bluetooth, text message, email, Facebook and more.

steps.text: From the Home screen, tap the Google folder.
Swipe up to see more options.

notes:
Note: 

For this tutorial, we're sharing photos with Bluetooth. You can select any available share option, but steps may vary slightly depending on what you choose.

Note: 

Make sure the device you're sending photos to has Bluetooth on and is set to be discoverable or visible.
Once another device is selected, your picture will automatically send.

tutorials.title: Subscribing to your favorite channels
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Subscribing to your favorite channels

If you like a youtube video you are watching, you can subscribe to their channel through the Youtube app.

steps.text: From a video on YouTube, tap the channel's name.

tutorials.title: Switching between calls
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Switching between calls

While on a phone call, you may receive a second phone call. You can put one phone call on hold and talk to other other and switch between them.

steps.text: From an ongoing call, swipe up to answer.
notes:
Note: 

This will put the original call on hold.

steps.text: To switch between calls, tap Swap
Tap the End icon on your current call to hang up and return to the other call.

tutorials.title: Syncing account contacts
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Syncing account contacts

Some accounts that you have on your device will allow you to sync contacts from the email address to your device.

steps.text: From Settings app, scroll to and tap Passwords, passkeys & accounts.
Tap or slide the Contacts switch to ON.

tutorials.title: Taking a picture
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Taking a picture

Pictures taken with your device will be saved in a gallery or photos app. You can adjust the settings of your device's camera before taking the picture.

steps.text: From the Home screen, tap the Camera icon.
notes:
Note: 

You can also access the Camera from the Lock screen by dragging the Camera icon up toward the top of the screen.

steps.text: Tap the Shutter icon to take a picture.

tutorials.title: Teaching kids how to call 911
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Teaching kids how to call 911

Teach your children how to dial 911 in the event of an emergency. They may need to know how to unlock your device.

steps.text: Press the Power button to wake up the phone.
Swipe the screen up to unlock the phone.
notes:
Note: 

If you have additional screen security set on your phone (e.g., a PIN), be sure to show your child how to unlock it.

steps.text: Show your child where the Call icon is, but don't tap it unless there's an emergency.
notes:
Note: 

You can also use Emergency Mode to extend your phone's battery life, call 911, send your location to a contact and more.

tutorials.title: Transferring content from your old device via wireless connection
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Transferring content from your old device via wireless connection

Using a wireless connection, you can move your pictures, videos, and other media files from your old device to your new device.

steps.text: On your other device, tap Set up to open the scanner, then scan the QR code to begin.
Tap Accept & continue, then continue through the following initial device setup steps as prompted.
To choose what apps and data to copy from your old device, tap Next.
Tap Copy, then continue through the remaining initial device setup steps to finish setting up your device.

tutorials.title: Transferring your eSIM and phone number after device setup
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Transferring your eSIM and phone number after device setup

This tutorial explains how to transfer your existing eSIM and phone number from an old device to a new one after the initial setup is complete.

steps.text: From the Settings app, tap Network & internet.
Tap Transfer a SIM from another device.
On your other device, follow the on-screen prompts.
notes:
Note: 

Make sure to enable a secure screen lock and are on the most recently released software version.

steps.text: On your other device follow the on-screen prompts.

tutorials.title: Transferring your eSIM and phone number during initial setup
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Transferring your eSIM and phone number during initial setup

This tutorial guides you through the process of transferring your existing eSIM and phone number to a new device during its initial setup. Perfect for users switching phones or activating a new device, this step-by-step guide shows how to move your mobile service seamlessly as part of the setup flow.

steps.text: From the Set up using another device screen within initial setup, tap Android device.
On your other device follow the on-screen prompts.
notes:
Note: 

Make sure to enable a secure screen lock and are on the most recently released software version.

steps.text: Verify the security with the code or password used on the device you are transferring from.
Enter your email or phone number for your Google sign in and then tap Next.
Enter your Google sign in password and then tap Next.

tutorials.title: Turning Airplane mode on and off
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Turning Airplane mode on and off

Airplane mode turns off cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth connections. (Note: You can manually turn Wi-Fi or Bluetooth back on while airplane mode is active.)
tutorials.category: Wi-Fi, Mobile Data, Bluetooth, and Browsers

steps.text: From the Settings app, tap Network & internet.
Tap or slide the Airplane mode switch to ON.
notes:
Note: 

You can also turn airplane mode on and off through the Notification panel.

tutorials.title: Turning Do Not Disturb on or off
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Turning Do Not Disturb on or off

Do Not Disturb (DND) allows users to silence incoming calls and notifications temporarily, sending them directly to voicemail or marking them as missed.

steps.text: From the Home screen, swipe down to open the Notification Panel.
Swipe down again to open Quick settings.
Tap Do Not Disturb to turn it on.
Tap Do Not Disturb again to turn it off.

tutorials.title: Turning autoplay off
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Turning autoplay off

When you are listening to music or watching videos, you can enable autoplay so that music or videos will keep playing.

steps.text: From the YouTube app You screen, tap the Settings icon.
Tap or slide the Autoplay next video switch to OFF.

tutorials.title: Turning off animations on your device
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Turning off animations on your device

You can turn off all on-screen animations on your device to help address any viewing issues you may be experiencing.

steps.text: From the Settings app, scroll to and tap Accessibility.
Tap or slide the Remove animations switch to ON.

tutorials.title: Turning on Spoken assistance accessibility options
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Turning on Spoken assistance accessibility options

Your device can speak the text you're typing if you need a little help with your keyboard inputs.

steps.text: From the Settings app, scroll to and tap Accessibility.
Tap or swipe the Select to Speak shortcut switch to ON.
To activate Select to Speak, swipe down to open the Notification Panel.
Swipe down again to open Quick Settings.
Drag your finger across any on screen text to select it.
notes:
Note: 

Your device will dictate the text within the highlighted box.

tutorials.title: Turning on Universal switch
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Turning on Universal switch

The Universal Switch feature allows you to control your device using an external switch, head movements, or face gestures.

steps.text: From the Settings app, scroll to and tap Accessibility.
Tap or slide the Use Switch Access access to ON.

notes:
Note: 

Follow the on screen steps to continue the switch setup.

tutorials.title: Turning on and changing Color adjustment settings
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Turning on and changing Color adjustment settings

You can modify your screen's colors to make it easier to distinguish one from another.

steps.text: From the Settings app, scroll to and tap Accessibility.
Select your preferred color correction mode.
Tap or slide the Use color correction switch to ON.

tutorials.title: Turning on and changing Flash notification settings
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Turning on and changing Flash notification settings

Your device can flash its camera light, or the screen itself, whenever you've received a new notification.

steps.text: From the Settings app, scroll to and tap Accessibility.
Scroll to and tap Flash notifications.
Tap or slide the Camera flash switch to ON.

tutorials.title: Turning on and changing Live Caption settings
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Turning on and changing Live Caption settings

With Live Caption, your device will automatically create captions for any audio that's currently playing, such as podcasts, music, and videos.

steps.text: From the Settings app, scroll to and tap Accessibility.
Tap or slide the Show captions switch to ON.

tutorials.title: Turning on and changing your Accessibility menu
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Turning on and changing your Accessibility menu

The Assistant Menu allows you access your device's hardware buttons and trigger gesture-based actions by tapping buttons on the screen.

steps.text: From the Settings app, scroll to and tap Accessibility.
Tap or swipe the Accessibility menu shortcut switch to ON.
To access the Accessibility Menu, tap the Accessibility Menu shortcut button.

tutorials.title: Turning on captions
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Turning on captions

Learn how to enable accessibility options in your favorite streaming app.

steps.text: From the YouTube app You screen, tap the Settings icon.
Tap or slide the Show captions switch to ON.

tutorials.title: Turning on purchase authentication in Google Play
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Turning on purchase authentication in Google Play

Learn how to enable purchase authentication to protect your account from fraudulent purchases.

steps.text: From the Play Store app main screen, tap the Account icon.

notes:
Note: 

If you are using Biometric verification, toggling your Biometric verification off and on forces the Play Store to re-register your fingerprint or face scan. This is highly effective if your phone keeps ignoring your biometric login attempts.

steps.text: Select your preferred purchase authentication setting, then tap OK.
notes:
Note: 

Temporarily changing this setting to Always forces Google Play to reset its security connection. This is a quick trick to kickstart the system if your screen is freezing or looping during checkouts.

steps.text: Enter your Google account password, then tap Verify.

tutorials.title: Turning your phone on and off
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Turning your phone on and off

Turning your device off and on is called "restarting" your device. Restarting your device is a common first step in troubleshooting any device issues. No saved information will be lost during a restart.

steps.text: To turn on the phone, press and hold the Power button.
To turn the phone off, press and hold the Power button.
notes:
Note: 

For your device, you may have to press Power and Volume Up.

tutorials.title: Uninstalling an app from Google Play
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Uninstalling an app from Google Play

Remove applications or widgets to free up space on your device. Once you remove an application or widget you will not be able to use it again unless you redownload it onto the device.

steps.text: From the Play Store app main screen, tap the Account icon.
Find and select the app you want to uninstall.

tutorials.title: Unlocking the screen
tutorials.intro:
Moto G - 2025
Unlocking the screen

Learn how to unlock the screen on your device. You can change your lock screen to have different types of security locks, including pattern, pin and password. Your device may automatically lock after a certain amount of time depending on your screen timeout settings. Ensure that you remember the code for unlocking your device; if you forget your unlock code you may lose the information on your device.

steps.text: From the Lock screen, swipe up to unlock your phone.
notes:
Note: 

For this tutorial, we're showing how to unlock the screen with a PIN. However, you may have a different type of screen security set up. If you don't have screen security set up, simply drag the Lock icon up to unlock it.
